column1: # scripts/stacks.tsv: one row per stack. Read through scripts/stacks.js, its one reader, by scripts/on-manifest-change.js (restore after a merge), scripts/format-changed.js (pre-push format check) and the project-init skill (scaffold). Commands run through the OS shell.

# Columns, tab-separated: stack | triggers: file patterns, space-separated, matched by path or basename | needs: a file that must exist at the root for the row to fire, or - | restore: command run from the repo root, or - | scaffold: commands joined by " && " with {Name} PascalCase, {name} kebab-case, {template} chosen by project-init, or - | formats: patterns of the files a push publishes that this row formats, or - | format: check-only command, {files} replaced by those paths, or - to skip. Fallbacks separated by " ?? " are tried in order until one tool is installed (the dotnet row prefers a project Husky.NET task runner, then dotnet format). It must not rewrite files; the hook reports and blocks, and git push --no-verify skips it. The formats cell is the contract and the format command trusts it, so the prettier rows pass no --ignore-unknown and an extension prettier cannot parse fails loudly; ADR-0003 is why, and which extensions that admits. The dotnet row loads the project first, so it costs 5-15s on a push touching C#: blank the cell to opt out. A row whose triggers are - only scaffolds: dotnet-aspire is the .NET scaffold for the microservices unit type, and the dotnet row restores and format-checks what it creates. | runner: the Gherkin runner the scaffold installs for the BDD stage (reqnroll, cucumber-js, pytest-bdd), or -. scripts/wire-acceptance.js points it at tests/features/, which scripts/bdd-features.js writes from docs/bdd/, and the acceptance workflow proves every row naming one, so a column that names a runner the script does not wire fails there. The .NET rows add Reqnroll.xUnit to an xunit project of the SDK's own rather than using Reqnroll's project template: the template targets net8.0 whatever SDK runs it, and the project reference to the library beside it is refused. The pnpm row allows esbuild's build with --allow-build: pnpm runs no dependency's install script until the project allows it, and from pnpm 12 an install that would have ignored one fails instead, so the allowance is recorded in pnpm-workspace.yaml when the scaffold runs.
